focus: Inspect tests/upgrade-legacy.vitest.ts and its harness to identify the measured work behind the roughly 400-second cli lane.
noveltyJustification: All three findings add previously undocumented details about sandbox resets, nested subprocess work, and the already-split CLI runner.
keyQuestions: Which fixture setup, waits, subprocesses, and assertions account for the roughly 400-second cli lane in tests/upgrade-legacy.vitest.ts, and what test-only changes can reduce elapsed time while retaining every assertion?
Which twelve timing-sensitive system-deep-loop files make up about 265 seconds, what shared-state or timing assumptions keep them serial, and can any safe scheduling change retain all assertions?
What accounts for about 300 seconds of import time in the spec-kit core lane, how is that time produced, and which test-process or module-loading changes can reduce it without changing coverage?
What evidence would justify production changes involving singleWriterReadCache or gateway rescans, and how should their runtime-behavior risk be separated from test-only speed work?
How do worker count and file parallelism affect elapsed time on smaller CI runners, and what runner-specific measurements should guide any concurrency change?
answeredQuestions: Which fixture setup, waits, subprocesses, and assertions account for the roughly 400-second cli lane in tests/upgrade-legacy.vitest.ts, and what test-only changes can reduce elapsed time while retaining every assertion?
ruledOut: Increasing the CLI project's file-level parallelism alone; the slow test file already runs beside the remaining CLI files, and its cases share a mutable sandbox.
